candidates.content: Covers Danish daily lives in the last 150 years, with exhibitions that both include artifacts relating to the main theme, and art portraying the life of the industrial worker.

candidates.price: Admission to the art museum: 45 kr, garden is free

candidates.name: Kastellet

candidates.price: Joint ticket for both the Zoological Museum and the Geological Museum 95 Kr, students 50 kr

candidates.price: Adults 110 kr, under 30 years 85 kr, under 18 years free

candidates.name: Music Museum
candidates.content: Trace the history of music, with a visit to Denmark’s most comprehensive collection of instruments from all over the world at the Danish Music Museum.

candidates.content: The country's only privately owned concert hall, featuring some interesting architecture as it has been fitted into some old stables. The programme mainly features classical Chamber music, with artists from all over Europe.

candidates.name: Copenhill
candidates.price: 150 kr/hour for skiing. Access to the rooftop bar is free
candidates.content: Ski slope on top of the huge "Amager Bakke" incineration plant. You can ski, hike, climb, walk up the steps, etc. Or you can just take the elevater up, order a drink at the rooftop bar and enjoy the great view of copenhagen.

candidates.name: Den Grå Hal

candidates.name: Cycle or walk over the Cykelslangen

candidates.name: Copenhagen Fashion Week

candidates.name: Stella Polaris

candidates.name: RAW

candidates.content: Cafe 5-oeren was established in 1991 and has its roots in the nearby free air concert venue, 5-oeren. Local and unsophisticated bar. Both smoking and non-smoking rooms.

candidates.name: Eiffel Bar

candidates.name: Halvandet

candidates.name: Cafe Kellerdirk

candidates.name: BrewPub

candidates.name: Club Mambo

candidates.name: Discotek In

candidates.name: Kulør Bar
candidates.content: A hit-or-miss sorta place, with nice colorful interiors, chill corners, and occasional artistic performances in the midst of the partying crowd. The entrance fee includes free beers from 22:00 to 01:00, Minimum age is 18 on Thursd

candidates.price: Set menu for 1048 kr, wines double the price

candidates.name: Morgenstedet
candidates.content: Morgenstedet is a vegetarian eatery, and all the food here is made from organic and fresh vegetables from a Danish farm. Nice outdoor seating along benches in the garden, and nice rustic interiors inside. The service is can be rea

candidates.content: Michelin starred French restaurant, open since 1976 and located in the oldest building in Copenhagen. The setting is amazing, with Gothic arches and a medieval atmosphere.

candidates.name: Ravelinen

candidates.content: Very traditional summer restaurant in townhouse from 1728, serving traditional Danish cuisine including smørrebrød, in either the beautiful building, or on an outdoor balcony with view over a canal.

candidates.name: Mio

candidates.content: The oldest of the Frederiksberg garden restaurants. The main building is from 1630. Serves very traditional Danish food in mix between a Garden and an outdoor German style Beer hale, but also has indoor seating. No music played

candidates.name: Krøgers Family Garden
candidates.content: Only dating back to 1864, this is the youngest of the family gardens, where you sit outside on long benches drinking beer while garbling in traditional Danish fare. Live music every weekend in the summer

candidates.name: Lagkagehuset
candidates.content: While the original "layer cake house" is in Christianshavn, the famous bakery, one of the best in Copenhagen, has expanded all over the city (and Denmark for that matter), with no less than five outlets in Indre By.

candidates.name: Perchs Tearoom
candidates.content: A classic tea room serving more than 150 different tea variants. In the tea room, there is also served different locale cakes and sandwiches. Tea has been served in this location since 1835.

candidates.name: Nybro Kro

candidates.price: All you can eat buffet 198 kr

candidates.content: The most popular of Copenhagen's flea markets, since the neighbourhood is rather affluent, you can often find good antiques and upscale secondhand fashion brands. Beers are often served from tents, and sometimes there is folksy li

candidates.name: Gourmand Ostespecialisten
candidates.content: Great cheese and other delicacies. Try their own "Sankt Thomas" cheese that is ripening in the cellars somewhere below Frederiksberg if you need a change from the regular Danish supermarket cheese. They also make great sandwiches

candidates.name: Lyngby Storcenter
candidates.content: A large shopping mall in central Lyngby, with more than 120 shops, restaurants and supermarkets over 34.100 m².

candidates.name: Holte midpunkt
candidates.content: Mall in central Holte with speciality stores, two supermarkets and a library with internet access on the 3rd floor.

december.text: Autumn and winter have a profound effect on the city. The vibrant summer life withers and the streets go quiet, as most Copenhageners go directly home from work. This is where the Danish concept of hygge sets in, roughly translating into cosiness. It is the local way of dealing with the short dark days. Friends and fam

Strøget is one of the largest pedestrian malls in the world which links City Hall, Kongens Nytorv, and Nørreport station. Impeccably dressed Copenhageners breeze through high-end fashion and design stores when not zig-zagging through the hordes of tourists during the summer and Christmas seasons. Your fellow visitors c

Nørrebro Flea Market is Denmark's longest and narrowest. It stretches for 333 m on one half of the sidewalk by the wall of the Assistens Cemetery on Nørrebrogade. Here you may find a Royal Porcelain Christmas Plate, a Chesterfield chair or plain or downright rubbish. Open from 4 April until 31 October on Saturdays 06:0

For breakfast and lunch try one of Copenhagen's bakeries (Bager — look for a pretzel-like contraption out front). They are numerous and the quality is excellent.
